The way I've always interpreted and played it is that the Isolated hero exists in a total vacuum.  Nothing that they do can have any impact on the experience of the other heroes, and nothing the other heroes do can have any impact on them.

 

any rules/questions are resolved this way (though you are of course free to make up your own interpretations):

For Non-isolated heroes:   The (H) value stays the same.  In all other respects, the Isolated Hero exists outside of their sphere of influence.  none of their cards, powers, ongoings, redirections, or choices can have ANY influence.  The isolated hero takes full damage, even if the villain is hypersoniced or stunned, and gets no bonus from things like bounties.

thematically, I resolve this as the Isolated hero has been detained, delayed, or ambushed.

The Isolated Hero may reduce the HP of the villain, because they are still attempting to re-unite with their friends.  If the villain is reduced to 0, all of the villain cards become a moot point, and it is assumed that they re-unite.  

In the event that Ms. Information ever gets any sort of last-second reprieve, or omnitron-like ability to stick around until all diversions have been handled, then Isolated hero would persist.

 

For the Isolated Hero:

Until the card is destroyed, they exist entirely on their own.  If they are the last one standing, the other heroes cannot use incap. powers on them (though they may still provide indirect aid by destroying ongoings/environments).  If they go down, they may not use direct incap powers on other heroes, as ongoings played on heroes persist after incapacitation- (see People V. Plague Rat).  They may provide indirect aid in the form of destroying non-hero ongoings/environments (or any other incap that does not proivide a direct benefit to heroes, or acts upon the villain).

The key difference for us when we play is that when an Isolated Hero is acting or being acted upon, we simply look at all the active effects in play at that time and ignore all those that generated from a Hero deck. Our disagreement centers around whether Isolated Hero prevents direct and indirect hero effect interactions, or if it only prevents direct interactions. I agree with you that, for a solid ruling, we need to work with the wording. I just do not see the wording of the card excluding indirect hero interactions.

By Any Means, Stun Bolt, and Ground Pound, as a set, represent the shades of that question very well.

By Any Means interacts with an Isolated Hero's instance of damage dealt. Should that be allowed? (I think certainly not)

Stun Bolt interacts with an instance of damage being dealt to the Isolated Hero. Should that be allowed? (I think no, but it's not clear admittedly)

Ground Pound interacts with the ability of the game to interact with the Isolated Hero. Should that be allowed? (Instinct says no, but leaning toward yes)

If theres an interaction between two hero effects and/or cards, whether directly or indirectly, the case can be made that they have indeed affected each other and would be explicitly banned by Isolated Hero. But the flood gates are open as to what consititues an interaction between hero effects/cards. You do not see Stun Bolts as a lasting debuff coming from Wraith, as I do, leading us to different views as to whether that is actually an interaction between two hero cards/effects at all.
